content.text: What Each Option Actually Offers

Crypto-native stacks (like COREMERCH's Complete Builder Kit) use blockchain payments and serverless infrastructure. You own the code, the hosting, and the data. Local gateways (bKash, Nagad) work only within Bangladesh—useless for international clients. Escrow services (Payoneer, Skrill) act as middlemen, holding your funds until you prove delivery. Peer-to-peer networks (Paxful, LocalBitcoins) connect you directly to buyers but require manual negotiation. The crypto-native stack wins for sovereignty: no middlemen, no geographic restrictions, no platform lock-in. You deploy your store on GitHub Pages or Cloudflare, accept 300+ cryptocurrencies via NOWPayments, and deliver files automatically. The tradeoff? You must understand basic web deployment—but that's a skill you own forever.
How They Handle Restricted Countries

Local payment gateways fail immediately for international clients. Escrow services often restrict accounts from countries like Ghana or Zimbabwe without warning. Peer-to-peer networks work but expose you to scams and volatile exchange rates. Crypto-native stacks remove geography entirely. A creator in Accra selling an eBook uses the same infrastructure as one in Dhaka selling a course. Cloudflare Workers handle backend logic, Supabase stores orders, and Google Drive delivers files. Payments confirm on-chain within minutes. No country-specific KYC. No frozen accounts. The architecture is borderless by design—because it's built on protocols, not platforms.
Payment Speed, Fees, and Real Costs

Local gateways process payments instantly but only within Bangladesh. Escrow services take 2–5 business days and charge 2–5% per transaction. Peer-to-peer networks are fast but add 5–15% in exchange rate markups. Crypto payments confirm in 5–30 minutes depending on the network. NOWPayments charges 0.5%—no monthly fees, no hidden costs. Recommended networks like BSC or Solana keep transaction fees under $0.10. The real cost? Escrow services hold your funds hostage. Peer-to-peer networks waste your time. Crypto-native stacks require an upfront investment in learning—but you own the infrastructure afterward. No subscriptions. No platform fees. No geographic barriers.
Crypto-native stacks remove geographic barriers entirely—your commerce is borderless.
Ownership, Automation, and Delivery

Local gateways and escrow services own your customer data. Peer-to-peer networks require manual delivery for every sale. Crypto-native stacks give you full ownership. Deploy once, sell forever. Orders store in your Supabase database. Files deliver automatically from Google Drive or Cloudflare R2. The moment payment confirms on-chain, the webhook fires—no human intervention. This is infrastructure sovereignty: you own the hosting, the backend logic, the payment processor, and the delivery mechanism. COREMERCH provides the blueprints and templates, but after deployment, they have no access. Your stack is yours.
Which Architecture to Choose Based on Your Situation

If you sell only to Bangladeshi clients, local gateways work—but limit your growth. If you trust middlemen holding your funds, escrow services are an option. If you have time to negotiate every sale, peer-to-peer networks might suffice. But if you want to own your commerce infrastructure, crypto-native stacks are the only choice. They require more upfront effort but deliver lifetime sovereignty. A creator in Lagos selling presets uses the same stack as one in Manila selling templates. Geography becomes irrelevant. Frequently Asked Questions
Can I use this stack if I’m not a developer?

Yes. The Complete Builder Kit includes templates and blueprints designed for non-developers. You’ll need to follow deployment instructions, but no coding is required. The stack uses free tools like Google Apps Script and GitHub Pages, which are beginner-friendly.
What if my buyers don’t use cryptocurrency?

NOWPayments generates payment links for 300+ cryptocurrencies. Buyers can pay using any wallet or exchange. You don’t need to educate them—the system handles it. Recommended networks like BSC and Solana keep fees under $0.10 per transaction.
How do I handle chargebacks or disputes?

Crypto transactions are irreversible, so chargebacks are impossible. For disputes, provide clear product descriptions and delivery proof. Since you own the infrastructure, you control the refund process—no platform policies to navigate.
What happens if Cloudflare or GitHub goes down?

Cloudflare and GitHub have 99.99% uptime. If an issue occurs, your data is stored in your Supabase database and Google Drive. You can redeploy to another provider without losing sales history or customer data.

The stack uses blockchain for payments but complies with local laws. You’re not operating an exchange—you’re accepting payments for digital goods. Always consult local regulations, but the architecture is designed to be geographically neutral.
